messages:
alex: Quick proposal — introduce a 'lease-window compaction' stage in the prefix/KV cache to reduce eviction thrash across tenants. TL;DR: group soft-pins into epoched windows, run a bounded compaction pass that rewrites residency metadata and coalesces pin ranges. Could cut churn when many small prefixes bounce.

morgan: Curious — how is this meaningfully different from demote+soft-evict we already have? :thinking:

alex: Good q. Demote currently marks items for later eviction but we still keep a lot of tiny sparse entries around. Lease-window compaction will explicitly: (1) collect contiguous soft-pins within an epoch, (2) atomically collapse them into a compact residency descriptor, (3) update the lease token mapping so handoffs are still replayable.

priya: Metric ask: what's the expected win and how do we measure regression? I'd want a 95th tail write-latency & evict-rate per-tenant before/after, plus change in prefix-count-per-slot.

alex: Agreed. Proposed metrics: `prefix.count`, `prefix.fragments`, `evict.ops`, `prefetch.misses`, plus a new `compaction.runs` counter and `compaction.duration_ms` histogram.

sam: Correctness: how do we maintain read-after-write guarantees during a compaction pass? If compaction rewrites residency metadata, readers might miss in-flight writes.

alex: Plan: compaction runs under a short-lived lease that quiesces new demotes to the next epoch. Reads consult two layers during transition: current residency map + pending compact delta. Pseudocode:

````
// compaction outline
lock(epoch)
collect = scan(prefixes in epoch)
compact = coalesce(collect)
apply_atomic(compact, token_update)
unlock(epoch)
````

Reads check `pending_compact[epoch]` if `token.version > compact.base_version`.

ira: Rollback story? If compaction corrupts a descriptor or exposes a bug, we need fast revert without full restart.

alex: Rollback options: (A) compaction is staged as write-ahead: write compact descriptor to a shadow slot and flip pointer only after full validation; (B) keep previous descriptor around as a tombstone until safe. We plan (A) for faster revert — pointer flip is single CAS.

morgan: How about multi-tenant safety — if many tenants share a slab, compaction for one tenant shouldn't increase eviction pressure for others.

alex: We'll limit compaction I/O & memory with per-slab compaction quotas and backpressure: `compaction.tokens` per-slab. If slab tokens exhausted, compaction yields. Also prefer compaction during low CPU windows.

priya: Testing plan? Want smoke, memcheck, and an end-to-end that simulates 10k small prefixes bouncing.

ira: Also add an invariants test: run compaction and then verify no prefix appears as both resident and demoted, and that rehydration path still finds data within X ms.

alex: Yep. Smoke plan: feature-flag gated rollout. Stage 1: perf-only runs on a small shard with `compaction.max_windows=1`. Stage 2: expands to 20% of nodes, enable additional defensive checks (validation hashes). Stage 3: global flip.

infra-bot: CI:compaction-smoke job queued for shard-12. link: https://ci.internal/compaction-smoke/1749994322

sam: One more nit — telemetry for compaction-caused eviction spikes. Add `evict.spike_after_compact` gauge (per-slab) so we can auto-roll back if spike > threshold.

alex: Added. Also API: runtime-config example to opt-in:

````
runtime:
  compaction:
    enabled: true
    max_windows: 2
    slab_token_limit: 8
    validation_hash: true
````

priya: Great. Any long-term refactor notes? This seems like a stepping stone toward an epoched-lease model where handoffs and compaction are first-class.

alex: Exactly — thinking long-term: collapse several ad-hoc demote primitives into a unified epoch-based lifecycle. This RFC follow-up would be the first incremental change toward that.

ira: Thanks. I can help draft the canary playbook + rollback runbook.

alex: Awesome — I'll put a short RFC doc + checklist in the repo and link here. Thanks all :thumbsup:
